trend_source: A UK-style story video about why rich people keep getting richer, using a three-layer money pyramid, pulled 88.3k views and 664 shares. The 'build the bottom layer first' idea clearly resonates.
title: The 3 money layers most Singaporeans never build
hooks: Most of us only ever live on the top layer of our money: it comes in, it goes straight back out.
Saving alone builds nothing if inflation quietly eats what you don't put to work.
Rich people don't just earn more. They build a bottom layer first.
talking_points: Layer one is the money that leaves as fast as it arrives: rent, food, lifestyle. Most people stop here.
The middle layer is your safety net: emergency savings and protection so one bad month doesn't wipe you out.
The bottom layer is assets that keep working while you sleep, built slowly through tools like CPF, SRS and long-term investing.
You don't need a fortune to start. You need to name which layer each dollar is going to.
cta: Comment LAYERS and I'll send you a simple way to map your three money layers this month.
why_it_works: The proven pyramid framing is simple and visual, and it honestly leads into cash flow, protection and long-term planning without overpromising.
how_to_film: Draw the three layers on paper or a tablet on camera. Open with the first hook straight to lens, then point to each layer as you explain. Keep it calm and under 40 seconds.

title: The credit card lesson nobody taught us at 18
hooks: At 18 I was handed a credit card with one instruction: use it if you need it. That was it.
There's a trap where you empty your bank account just to pay last month's card bill.
A credit card is borrowed money, even when it doesn't feel like it.
talking_points: With no guidance, it's easy to spend to the limit and spend the next month just catching up.
Working only to pay off the card is exhausting and quietly steals your future savings.
The rule that fixes it: if you can't pay the statement in full, you can't afford the purchase.
Build a small buffer first so the card is a convenience, not a monthly trap.
cta: Share this with someone getting their first card so they skip the lesson the hard way.
why_it_works: A locally proven, honest personal story about debt gives the advisor instant credibility on a relatable money mistake.
